claims.text: The starting material is an Mg-containing lightweight high-entropy alloy in a metastable solid-solution-plus-intermetallic state.
High-temperature annealing is the proposed intervention.
The annealing temperature should be above 500 °C.
High-temperature annealing will reduce the amount of intermetallic compounds.
High-temperature annealing will improve solid-solution stability.
The intervention operates through thermally activated diffusion.
Annealing will increase hardness by 10% relative to the as-processed state.
Annealing will reduce corrosion rate by 20% relative to the as-processed state.
Annealing will improve oxidation resistance by 15% relative to the as-processed state.
The alloy density must remain below 6 g/cm3.
Annealing time from 1 to 10 hours and temperature from 500 to 700 °C may produce composition- and processing-history-dependent variability.
Microstructure, hardness, corrosion rate, and oxidation behavior will be measured after annealing at 500, 600, and 700 °C for 1, 5, and 10 hours.

contradictions.description: The mediator predicts a reduction of intermetallic compounds, while precipitation is named as the mechanism without explaining why precipitation would dissolve rather than create or increase secondary/intermetallic phases.
The condition specifies a temperature above 500 °C, but the stated range and experiment include 500 °C itself.
